chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: The Henderson dance: a Colored dance, and Hodges commuting to New York
summary: The Henderson band played a White dance first and the Colored dance after midnight; Holmes explains Hodges's back-and-forth work with Bechet in Harlem clubs.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you go to that thing...? Was Carney there? Was Howard Johnson there? Johnny Hodges? Everybody went?
Well, I don't know if anyone of them particularly were there. But all the... You know, musicians and everybody else went. Yeah, I guess...
And it was a dance?
No, we didn't go with no band. No.
It was a dance that they played?
It was a dance, yeah. And we went as...
And there was no segregation at that dance or anything?
It was a Colored dance.
Oh, it was a Colored dance.
Yeah. See, they had played a White dance
Holmes (10/9) - 24

for about four hours before. And this dance, I think they came in around 1 o'clock, 12 or 1 o'clock. That other dance was out in the country somewhere, but this dance was in the city. They only played one hour.
Then before that, Hodges was playing with a little group, so that the people there had...
As a fill-in, yeah. He was with a pick-up band.
So that must have been one of the first times for Hodges, too, to hear Armstrong.

Well, I can say so. Well, I don't know. Because see, at that time Johnny was back and forth into New York and back. See, his family was still in Boston, and he'd run over here and he'd play with Bechet in different clubs and things for a few weeks and so, and months; then he'd run back to Boston. He was back and forth.
So chances are he'd already been to the Roseland.

I don't know if he went to the Roseland. He was working uptown in Harlem then. I don't know whether he went downtown or anything like that. But he was interested in blowin' his horn. And he loved to blow it! He played at practically all these clubs around there. Bechet had a club, and then there was a place called the Garden of Joy on Seventh Avenue. Oh, there was a lot of
Holmes (10/9) - 25
clubs around then.
